meta.title_plain: How a boy who explored caves invented Mario and Zelda
meta.teaser: Shigeru Miyamoto turned his childhood adventures into the world's most famous games.

page.title: How a boy who explored caves invented Mario and Zelda
page.bigIdea: Shigeru Miyamoto didn't copy other games. He turned his own real-life adventures into play, and the whole world joined in.

cards.title: The kid who explored everything
cards.front: He was born in 1952 in Sonobe, Japan.
cards.back: As a boy, he explored fields, woods and caves near his home. Once, on a hike, he found a hidden lake. It felt like a real adventure.
cards.tryit: Walk somewhere near home you've never really looked at. Spot three new things.

cards.title: Toys got him hired
cards.front: He studied industrial design at art college.
cards.back: He first dreamed of drawing manga. In 1977, he showed his toy creations to Nintendo's president and got a job as an apprentice.
cards.tryit: Sketch a toy or gadget you wish existed. Label three parts.

cards.title: Jumpman becomes Mario
cards.front: His first big hit was Donkey Kong in 1981.
cards.back: The hero was first called "Jumpman." Later, Nintendo named him Mario, after the landlord of its warehouse. A name can change. The idea stays.
cards.tryit: Invent a hero for a game. Give them a simple nickname based on what they do.

cards.title: A cave becomes Zelda
cards.front: The Legend of Zelda came out in 1986.
cards.back: He based it on exploring the countryside as a kid. The first screen shows a cave, just like his memory. Inside, you get a sword.
cards.tryit: Draw a map of a secret area in your favourite Roblox or Fortnite world.

cards.title: Ideas are everywhere
cards.front: Mario has sold over 800 million games.
cards.back: He kept finding ideas in normal life. Gardening with his wife led to Pikmin. His dog Pikku inspired Nintendogs.
cards.tryit: Pick one hobby, like tennis. Write one game idea that comes from it.

words.d: Designing everyday objects, like toys, so they look good and work well.
A beginner who learns a job by working with experts.
A big series of games, films or books with the same characters.
In games, a maze-like area full of puzzles, enemies and treasure.

quiz.q: What did Miyamoto show Nintendo to get his job?
quiz.hint: Think about what he studied at college.
quiz.why: He studied industrial design, so he showed the toys he had designed.

quiz.q: What was Mario's first name in Donkey Kong?
quiz.hint: Think about what the hero does over barrels.
quiz.why: He was called Jumpman because jumping was his main move.

quiz.q: Where did the idea for Zelda come from?
opts: His childhood exploring caves and woods
quiz.hint: Look back at the first card.
quiz.why: Zelda recreates the feeling of exploring that he loved as a boy.

quiz.q: Which game was inspired by his dog?
quiz.why: His Shetland Sheepdog, Pikku, inspired Nintendogs in 2005.

page.think: Miyamoto turned exploring caves into Zelda. What moment from your own life, like a big tennis match, could you turn into a game?
